rules.sentence: Stress-induced changes in gut motility can manifest as diarrhea or constipation, whereas increased visceral sensitivity may contribute to symptoms such as irritable bowel syndrome.

Dysregulation of the gut-brain axis, mediated by stress, exacerbates gastrointestinal disorders and can worsen symptoms through bidirectional communication between the central nervous system and the gut microbiota.[17]
Prolonged exposure to elevated levels of cortisol can lead to muscle wasting and decreased bone density by inhibiting osteoblast activity and promoting osteoclast function.
